_read: Expectation cases read from the book by hand. Each has a page number, and the expectation is read FROM THE BOOK - never from the app's own data or the implementation. test_golden.js runs every case against all surfaces: price, resolver, card, fleet view and save round trip. A case does not start from 'does the code work' but from 'what does the book say'.
_list: Every case names a fleet list, because the same ship can be on several lists at a different price and with different required upgrades. The unit is created with addUnit() as in the app. The list '-' means a ship that is not bought from any list (a profile check only).
_status: gap = known to be missing; the case is written BEFORE the fix and it gets red until the task is done. If a gap case passes, that is reported too: then the task is done and the status must be updated.
_expect: points, hits, shields, turrets, speed, turns, armour, weapon_rows (the table's rows), active_weapons (the ones in force), weapon {match, range, fp, arc}, weapon_count {match, n} (instances in force), card_contains, card_lacks, exclusive_group_blocks, upgrade_offered / upgrade_not_offered (a list upgrade offered to this ship, a regex of the name), weapon_none {match, range} (no row in force with the name+range), card_count [{match, n}] (occurrences of a literal string in the card's HTML; for a star fort the pair base card + rule card), weapon_zones {quadrant, basilica} (the groups of the resolved weapon rows, p.110/500), view_contains / view_lacks (fleet view), roster_contains / roster_lacks (roster), n (the number in a squadron or of bought pieces, also on a hull-less row)
